newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end firmer on rise in bonds.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end firmer on rise in bonds.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures closed the day session firmer on Wednesday on the back of gains in long-term yen bond futures.
But nearby contracts failed to rise as much as distants did due to the higher key interbank overnight call rate.
The benchmark cash rate in the short-end of the money market was mainly traded at 0.51 percent on Wednesday, which was the highest level since October 1 last year.

The rise in the key overnight rate from Tuesday"s weighted average of 0.50 percent was mainly attributed to some banks" strong demand for short-term funds amid a lack of issues of long-term certificates of deposit (CD) lately.

In yen interest rate swaps, foreigners received three- to four-year fixed rates while paying floating rates in the afternoon and those who traded with them bought TIFFE Euroyen futures to hedge, traders said. That helped send the key December Euroyen futures higher to 99.27, they said.
The key December contract ended up 0.02 at 99.27. It moved in a range of 99.24 and 99.27 in turnover of 28,856 contracts.
"If the December breaks above 99.29, stop-loss buying may be triggered, resulting in a rise as high as 99.32," said a trust bank dealer.
But a further rise in the contract was unlikely unless the Bank of Japan (BOJ) changed its current record-low interest-rate policy, traders said.
Some traders said caution over prices shown in the afternoon by Yasuo Matsushita, governor of the Bank of Japan, might suggest the BOJ is preparing for higher interest rates.
But others disagreed, saying the bank would not raise interest rates before the end of this year, if then.
Matsushita told a news conference that domestic prices did not show signs of moving onto an upward trend.
However, he also said that the weak yen had "speeded up the tempo of the rise in prices of imports and we need to carefully watch domestic prices from now on."
The BOJ"s neutral operation in the morning failed to tame recent upward pressure in the key overnight rate, traders said.

The yield curve flattened as the overnight rate rose to 0.51 percent while long-end benchmark three-month CD rate was unchanged at 0.54. The issued volume of the CDs was a small 20 billion yen. -- Risa Maeda Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
